newsitem.title: USA: ATHLETICS-JONES DEFLECTS COMPARISON TO LEWIS.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-JONES DEFLECTS COMPARISON TO LEWIS.

text.p: Suddenly America again has a world-class athlete who excels in the sprints and long jump. But don't call Marion Jones the female Carl Lewis.

The 21-year-old Jones quickly deflected that moniker Sunday after winning the women's long jump to complete a 100-meter/long jump golden double at the U.S. athletics championships this week -- a performance that produced the year's leading result in both events.
"It's a great comparison, but my name is Marion Jones, not Carl Lewis," she said. "I'm a different type competitor."
Basketball and athletics have been her avenues to success, just like the woman she defeated Sunday, her idol Jackie Joyner-Kersee.
Both played basketball in college, and now as the 35-year-old Joyner-Kersee nears the end of her illustrious athletics career, Jones appears destined to take her place.
"I've always admired her, even when she was in high school," Joyner-Kersee said of Jones, who overtook her to claim the U.S. long jump crown Sunday.
"It's obvious that Marion has great talent," Joyner-Kersee said. "She's fast, she's strong, she has the jumping ability. Put all three combinations together and you are going to have great distance.
"Her presence only makes the rest of us better."
High praise from one of the greatest U.S. athletes of all time.
